1. If this is your first time, please read our contributor guidelines: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/first-contribution.md#your-first-contribution and developer guide https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/development.md#development-guide
2. Please label this pull request according to what type of issue you are addressing, especially if this is a release targeted pull request. For reference on required PR/issue labels, read here:
https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-release/release.md#issuepr-kind-label
3. Ensure you have added or ran the appropriate tests for your PR: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-testing/testing.md
4. If you want *faster* PR reviews, read how: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#best-practices-for-faster-reviews
5. If the PR is unfinished, see how to mark it: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#marking-unfinished-pull-requests
-->

**What type of PR is this?**

<!--
Add one of the following kinds:
/kind bug
/kind cleanup
/kind documentation
/kind feature
/kind design

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:
/kind api-change
/kind deprecation
/kind failing-test
/kind flake
/kind regression
-->

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
`PIDPressure` ahead of time to avoid other pods of the node being unable to use PID.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/98206

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
<!--
If no, just write "NONE" in the release-note block below.
If yes, a release note is required:
Enter your extended release note in the block below. If the PR requires additional action from users switching to the new release, include the string "action required".

For more information on release notes see: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/release-notes.md
-->
```release-note
action required: Add default Linux's eviction-hard to pid.available=10%, not configured pid.available Users of will be affected. 
If the available pid of the node (Linux) is lower than the 10% threshold, some pods will be evicted. 
The cluster administrator can refer to check whether the node workload reaches the threshold.
```

**Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.**:

<!--
This section can be blank if this pull request does not require a release note.

When adding links which point to resources within git repositories, like
KEPs or supporting documentation, please reference a specific commit and avoid
linking directly to the master branch. This ensures that links reference a
specific point in time, rather than a document that may change over time.

See here for guidance on getting permanent links to files: https://help.github.com/en/articles/getting-permanent-links-to-files

Please use the following format for linking documentation:
- [KEP]: <link>
- [Usage]: <link>
- [Other doc]: <link>
-->
```docs
1. PID based eviction: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/policy/pid-limiting/#pid-based-eviction
2. Eviction Signals: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/out-of-resource/#eviction-signals 
```
/release-note-none
/kind bug
/sig node

So this is a fairly significant operational change to a cluster, right?  After upgrade to a version with this code, workloads that were running within 10% of the max would start being evicted?  How would an administrator know that ahead of time?  What preparatory actions should an admin take before the upgrade?  These are questions I'd expect to see answered in both release notes and "pre-upgrade procedures".  Do we have an estimate of the percentage of clusters in the world this would impact after upgrade (i.e. how many people are in this state now as part of normal operations)?

> So this is a fairly significant operational change to a cluster, right? After upgrade to a version with this code, workloads that were running within 10% of the max would start being evicted? How would an administrator know that ahead of time? What preparatory actions should an admin take before the upgrade? These are questions I'd expect to see answered in both release notes and "pre-upgrade procedures". Do we have an estimate of the percentage of clusters in the world this would impact after upgrade (i.e. how many people are in this state now as part of normal operations)?

Not configured `pid.available` Users of will be affected, others will be ignored.
If the [available pid of the node (Linux)](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/out-of-resource/#eviction-signals) is lower than the `10%` threshold, some pods will be evicted.

The cluster administrator can refer to check whether the node workload reaches the threshold.
```shell
$ curl -s -k --key /etc/certs/kubelet-client.key --cert /etc/certs/kubelet-client.crt  https://10.6.125.8:10250/stats/summary|jq .node.rlimit.curproc/.node.rlimit.maxpid

0.0066375732421875
```
Before upgrading, the load of such nodes should be reduced as much as possible, so as to avoid driving behavior.

If cluster enhancement has been done for kubelet or `kernel.pid_max` is large enough, it will not be affected.
I found that `AliCloud`, `GCP` and `Daocloud` manufacturers have all strengthened.
The users who are affected are those who have not strengthened the reliability of their nodes. Therefore, their node reliability will be improved.

@Cweiping I think what @smarterclayton is suggesting is not to explain how to do it, but instead make sure we made enough preparatory actions to avoid breaking customers on upgrade.

Actions might include:

- [ ] Update release notes on this PR with an additional [action required](https://www.kubernetes.dev/docs/guide/release-notes/#applying-a-release-note:~:text=For%20pull%20requests%20that%20require%20additional,(case%20insensitive)%20in%20the%20release%20note%3A) note explaining what have changed.
- [ ] Documentation is updated: https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/26255. Is this PR closed intentionally?
- [ ] Think of more places this additional documentation you listed may be beneficial to be added to make sure the upgrade instructions are clear. Maybe this page https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/policy/pid-limiting/#m-docs-concepts-policy-pid-limiting . Also that page has a [note about pid_max](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/policy/pid-limiting/#m-docs-concepts-policy-pid-limiting:~:text=limit%20to%20a%20low%20default%2C%20such%20as%2032768) that also may be helpful to mention with the introduction of this feature.

Thank @SergeyKanzhelev and @smarterclayton review. I have updated the release note and website documents. I have updated the related documents of this feature. Is there any todo. Do you want to upgrade this PR to a feature to attract users' attention?

Associated Doc PR: https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/26261

this closed due to inactivity, but in case it gets picked back up, I strongly second @smarterclayton's comment at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/98207#issuecomment-784350321

having the control available seems useful, but defaulting it more restrictive than current behavior does not seem generally safe. A change like this deserves a tracking KEP to surface action-required items and upgrade considerations to consumers of a new kubernetes release.

What would it look like to default this to something much closer to the edge (e.g. 1%) or not have it active by default (0%)?

issue_context.title: Default not support PIDPressure of DefaultEvictionHard
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
`Kubelet` starts the evict pod only when PID resources are exhausted. At this point, other pods of nodes may have been affected, especially computing applications.

**What you expected to happen**:

`PIDPressure` ahead of time to avoid other pods of the node being unable to use PID.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

According to the default configuration:

```yaml
# kubelet
maxPods: 110
podPidsLimit: -1
```
```
# kernel
kernel.pid_max: 32678
```

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.18
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): CentOS Linux release 7.6.1810 (Core)
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:
